about: Read by AFK Realm (https://github.com/aspollon/AFK-Realm) when it builds the server. Without AFK Realm, apply the patches by hand: see README.md.

patches.name: Bots keep their bags
patches.why: mod-playerbots empties the bags of every random bot every 10 to 40 minutes and after every death. Without this change the bots never have anything to sell. Food, drink and potions are still renewed.

patches.name: Bots leave junk and food on the corpse
patches.why: Random bots picked up every grey item, every food and drink and every configured kind of junk, so their bags filled with vendor trash and they kept walking to vendors. The loot filter keeps those items on the corpse; quest items and the always-loot list still pass.

patches.name: Bots gather on slopes
patches.why: mod-playerbots ignores every vein and herb that lies more than 3.5 yards above or below the bot. Veins are in hillsides, so miners never mined. Now the height may grow with the distance.

patches.name: Bots go for the veins and herbs they see
patches.why: mod-playerbots only gathers what lies within the distance a bot walks for a corpse. A gatherer now goes for every vein and herb in sight, as a player follows the dots on the minimap.

patches.name: One answer to WTS, not fifty
patches.why: mod-playerbots lets every bot that hears "WTS [item]" whisper a price it does not mean. With deals by chat enabled, the few bots that really want the item answer instead.

patches.name: Hand-to-hand trades are the module's
patches.why: A deal agreed on by chat can be traded in person. mod-playerbots would run its own rules on that trade window (and cancel or accept it by its own prices); for a bot the module is trading for, it stands back.

patches.name: A bot spec roll can no longer stop the world
patches.why: mod-playerbots rolls a random talent spec with urand(1, sum of the spec probabilities). A custom class or an incomplete config can leave that sum at 0; the core asserts on urand(1, 0) and stops the worldserver. The patch keeps spec 0 and logs a warning instead, and guards the Druid bear/cat roll the same way.

patches.name: Bot loot logging cannot read a stale item
patches.why: mod-playerbots 2.6 added a bot loot log that dereferences the Item* on every loot, even when no playerbots.loot logger is configured. A merged or already removed loot item then ended the worldserver in Item::GetTemplate. The patch adds AiPlayerbot.LootLog (off by default) and checks the logger before touching the item.

patches.name: The crash races stay excluded
patches.why: A shorter AiPlayerbot.CrashingBotRaces value in a server config replaced the module author's list, so a race known to crash clients could be chosen again for random bots. The patch always adds 32,72,77,97 and lets the config add more races.

patches.name: Mystic Enchants use the core's two-argument guide
patches.why: The Zyth45 Playerbots 2.7 branch calls AscensionMysticEnchant::ApplyGuide with a third argument that the current CoA core does not have. The module passes the build's enchant list with the core's own signature instead, so Warcraft Reborn bots keep their Mystic Enchants and the server compiles.

patches.name: No Bloodforged gear while it is switched off
patches.why: Bloodforged.Enable = 0 only stops CoA's extra Bloodforged drops; the items stay in some loot tables and in the item store the bots are geared from. Bots wore them on realms without Bloodforged, often with models the client cannot show. While the switch is off, bots are not geared with them, do not put them on, and a re-gear replaces the ones they wear.

patches.name: Loot hooks only see an item that is really stored
patches.why: The core hands the raw Item* from StoreNewItem to every OnPlayerLootItem hook. A bot loot can leave that pointer stale when the stack is merged or the item is gone, and hooks that read it (the playerbots loot log) crash the worldserver. The patch calls the hooks only when the item is still in the player's inventory.

settings.why: Bots only gather ore and herbs they pass within this distance. With the default of 15 yards hardly any reach the auction house.
Bots were handed better gear at every level-up, so none ever needed anything from the auction house - and sold the old pieces to a vendor.
New bots start in uncommon gear at most. Rare gear becomes something worth buying.
In a group, bots roll need on what is an upgrade for them.
mod-playerbots' own chatter - a report of every quest and kill, dungeon suggestions, canned replies - is replaced by the personalities of this module.
